transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

People at work are plotting against me and changing my routes on purpose, and no one believes me when I tell them it’s happening. They are secretly altering my maps to make me look incompetent, but my boss and my husband just write it off as computer glitches. It is so frustrating that everyone thinks I'm the one making mistakes when I know they are doing this to me.
How long have you been feeling that people at work are plotting against you and changing your routes? Did this start suddenly over days to weeks, or has it been going on for months or longer?

The intense feeling that they are plotting and changing my routes has really taken over in just the last couple of months, though it started as a nagging suspicion. But looking back, I've felt off, struggled at work, and pulled away from everyone for about a year now, ever since I took on that lead role.

Besides believing your coworkers are sabotaging you, have you been hearing voices or noticing things others don’t, or has your speech or behavior felt disorganized to you or others? If so, when did those symptoms start compared with the suspiciousness?

I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there, but I do freeze up at my desk or pace the hallways muttering routes to myself. These behavioral struggles and feeling "off" have been building for about a year, whereas the clear sense that they are plotting against me only took over in the last couple of months.

Over the past year, before the belief that coworkers were plotting against you became strong, did you have a clear decline in your daily functioning—like trouble keeping up at work, less motivation or emotion, or your thoughts becoming hard to organize? Or were you otherwise functioning pretty normally aside from the suspicious belief?

Yes, my performance definitely slipped about a year ago when I started falling behind on routes and making mistakes, which I just blamed on burnout. Around that same time, I lost all motivation and stopped going to choir, softball, and church, and I completely withdrew from my husband and chores. All of that apathy and struggle started long before I realized they were actually plotting against me a couple of months ago.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent persecutory delusions, behavioral disturbance, and a clear prodromal/negative-symptom decline in functioning lasting about a year, with active psychotic symptoms emerging over the last couple of months. This pattern is most consistent with paranoid schizophrenia rather than an isolated delusional disorder, because there is broader deterioration, social withdrawal, apathy, and disorganized/catatonic-like behavior beyond a circumscribed delusion.
